public_comment.topic: Urges the boards to pursue a Proposition 2½ override for all town departments, warns time is running out to educate voters.

Says the runway to educate town meeting is critical; urges a multi-year (3-5 year) financial projection be presented so voters know how long an override will last, given how contract, health insurance and transportation costs are trending.

Praises the transparency of this budget season; urges putting storm water back into the budget rather than removing it, and recommends the town buy a GIS subscription so it stops paying consultants to remake the same maps.

Questions whether even the highest override tier truly buys two years of level service, warns fear-based messaging has an expiration date, and again urges a multi-year projection and cost-per-home examples for the messaging campaign.

minutes.headline: TriBoard formally voted to pursue a two-tier (not single-number) FY27 override, dropping stormwater from it
minutes.summary: The Select Board, Finance Committee and School Committee met jointly to finalize the structure and dollar figures of a Proposition 2½ override for the May town meeting and ballot, after months of separate budget work. They voted to pursue a two-tier override rather than one number, agreed to pull a stormwater utility request out of the override for now, and the School Committee raised its lower-tier ask to 1.6 million; officials could not guarantee the higher tier would prevent another override request next year, and the boards turned to planning joint public messaging before adjourning.

what_happened.line: The Select Board, Finance Committee and School Committee voted unanimously to pursue a two-tier FY27 override rather than a single override number.
The boards pulled stormwater out of the tier-two override and chose not to bring a standalone stormwater override article this cycle, deferring to the stormwater task force.
The School Committee raised its lower-tier override ask to restore fifth-grade band, leaving the higher tier unchanged.
Officials said they could not guarantee the higher override tier would avoid another override request next year, citing volatile costs like health insurance.
The boards agreed to bring in a paid communications professional to help plan joint messaging for town meeting and the ballot.

why_it_matters: A two-tier override means voters may face a choice between two different tax-bill impacts rather than one number, decided at May town meeting and on the ballot.
The lower tier's dollar figure now includes restoring fifth-grade band, and stormwater funding was pulled out of the override question entirely for now.
The boards themselves said the top tier is not guaranteed to be the last override ask, which residents should weigh alongside whatever figures appear in town-meeting materials.
